needs.proposedSignature: face declaration `exploit: true` (with a `covers` kind `by: 'exploit'` for the printed `^exploit$` line) + trigger event `{ on: 'exploits', self: true }`
needs.semantics: `exploit: true` installs the keyword's own ability: 'When this creature enters, you may sacrifice a creature' - a `may` over a `sacrifice` the controller chooses, the source itself being a legal choice. When that sacrifice actually happens the engine raises an `exploits` event whose source is the exploiting creature and whose triggering object is the sacrificed creature, so `{ on: 'exploits', self: true }` abilities fire once and can read the sacrificed creature as `triggering` / `that`. The event must NOT fire for ordinary sacrifices - that is exactly what makes `{ on: 'sacrifice' }` an unusable substitute today.
needs.clause: Exploit / When ~ exploits a creature, you may search your library for a card, put it into your hand, then shuffle.
